AUTHOR: Ayyagari
TITLE: Detecting Unexpected Marine Species with Underwater Cameras and Deep Learning
REGION: Marine refuge off Newfoundland, Canada (400-500 m); OzFish (Australia) for calibration
SPECIES: Seen: Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua), roughhead grenadier (Macrourus berglax); unseen: thorny skate, redfish, wolffish, halibut, spinytail skate, whelk, etc.
DATA: DFO baited deep-sea video (221 x 5-min videos, exhaustively annotated); OzFish crops as unseen-class calibration
V_EV: [V1 recoded NR on verification: statement not about the study's own water clarity] Sec. I: 'Inexpensive video cameras equipped with light sources and bait were placed at depths ranging from 400 to 500 meters'
D_EV: Sec. III: 'These 221 videos were divided into train, calibration, and test splits in approximately a 70-15-15 ratio'
R_EV: Sec. III: test set 'consists of segmented fish from the seen classes within 15% of the videos in the test split' (DFO data only; OzFish used for threshold calibration)
C_EV: Sec. V.C: 'Calculate the accuracy for each threshold and determine the threshold t* that yields the highest accuracy'; 'optimal thresholds of 0.60 and 0.75'
E_EV: Table III: 'Accuracy(%) on Seen Classes ... Unseen Classes ... Entire Test Set' only
ARCH: ViT and ResNet18 feature extractors + kNN with nearest-neighbour distance ratio (NNDR) open-set rule
NOTE: Open-set classification of fish crops from deep baited cameras. Split by video for seen classes; unseen-class test crops drawn from all splits (classes never used in training). OzFish (BRUV, Australia) used only as unseen-class examples for threshold calibration, not as an external test -> R1=N. NNDR threshold swept 0-1 and chosen by max validation accuracy (C_ALL P, C4 Y). NIMG = sum of Table I images (121,869). Trained 'with no pre-training'.
AUTHORS_FULL: D. Ayyagari; C. Morris; J. Barnes; C. Whidden
